{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzannB3fUjnetAZVhRKc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WftBtkkbSBpge6KFprwjuc","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261012-111947/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-cc-medium_cuda_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr unsigned int INF = 1000000000;\nconstexpr unsigned int MAX_DISTANCE = 200;\n\n// Edge length of a square tile. Each tile is handled by one thread block of\n// TILE x TILE threads, one thread per matrix cell.\nconstexpr size_t TILE = 32;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                     \\\n    do {                                                                     \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                           \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                           \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                               \\\n            exit(1);                                                         \\\n        }                                                                    \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Index calculation for flattened 2D array\ninline constexpr size_t idx2(const size_t i, const size_t j, const size_t n) noexcept {\n    return j * n + i;\n}\n\nvoid initializeDistanceMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes,\n                              const unsigned int rangeMin, const unsigned int rangeMax) {\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - rangeMin) + 1.0;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes * numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[i] = rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n    }\n\n    // Set diagonal to zero (distance from node to itself is 0)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid initializePathMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            path[idx2(i, j, numNodes)] = j;\n            path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = i;\n        }\n        path[idx2(j, j, numNodes)] = j;\n    }\n}\n\n// Phase 1: the diagonal tile (K,K). Runs the k-steps of round K inside the tile.\n// Before each k-step it saves the diagonal's column k and row k so that the\n// other tiles of this round can read the values d[.][k] and d[k][.] exactly as\n// they were before step k.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TILE * TILE)\nfwPhase1(unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path, unsigned int* colSnap, unsigned int* rowSnap,\n         const size_t m, const size_t K) {\n    __shared__ unsigned int tDist[TILE][TILE];\n    __shared__ unsigned int tPath[TILE][TILE];\n\n    const size_t ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t base = K * TILE;\n    const size_t gIdx = (base + ty) * m + base + tx;\n\n    tDist[ty][tx] = dist[gIdx];\n    tPath[ty][tx] = path[gIdx];\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < TILE; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int distIK = tDist[ty][kk];\n        const unsigned int distKJ = tDist[kk][tx];\n        if (tx == 0) colSnap[(base + ty) * TILE + kk] = distIK;\n        if (ty == 0) rowSnap[kk * m + base + tx] = distKJ;\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n        if (newDist < tDist[ty][tx]) {\n            tDist[ty][tx] = newDist;\n            tPath[ty][tx] = static_cast<unsigned int>(base + kk);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    dist[gIdx] = tDist[ty][tx];\n    path[gIdx] = tPath[ty][tx];\n}\n\n// Phase 2: tiles (K,J) for J != K (blockIdx.y == 0) and tiles (I,K) for I != K\n// (blockIdx.y == 1), blockIdx.x holds the other block index. Each of these tiles\n// reads one operand from the diagonal snapshot (fixed for the round) and the\n// other operand from its own, sequentially updated, contents.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TILE * TILE)\nfwPhase2(unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path, unsigned int* colSnap, unsigned int* rowSnap,\n         const size_t m, const size_t K) {\n    const size_t t = blockIdx.x;\n    if (t == K) return;\n    const bool isRowTile = (blockIdx.y == 0);\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int tDist[TILE][TILE];\n    __shared__ unsigned int tPath[TILE][TILE];\n    __shared__ unsigned int tFixed[TILE][TILE];\n\n    const size_t ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t rowBase = isRowTile ? K * TILE : t * TILE;\n    const size_t colBase = isRowTile ? t * TILE : K * TILE;\n    const size_t gIdx = (rowBase + ty) * m + colBase + tx;\n\n    tDist[ty][tx] = dist[gIdx];\n    tPath[ty][tx] = path[gIdx];\n    // Row tile: d[i][k] for the rows of block K. Column tile: d[k][j] for the columns of block K.\n    tFixed[ty][tx] = isRowTile ? colSnap[(rowBase + ty) * TILE + tx]\n                               : rowSnap[ty * m + colBase + tx];\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < TILE; ++kk) {\n        unsigned int distIK;\n        unsigned int distKJ;\n        if (isRowTile) {\n            distIK = tFixed[ty][kk];\n            distKJ = tDist[kk][tx];\n            if (ty == 0) rowSnap[kk * m + colBase + tx] = distKJ;\n        } else {\n            distIK = tDist[ty][kk];\n            distKJ = tFixed[kk][tx];\n            if (tx == 0) colSnap[(rowBase + ty) * TILE + kk] = distIK;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n        if (newDist < tDist[ty][tx]) {\n            tDist[ty][tx] = newDist;\n            tPath[ty][tx] = static_cast<unsigned int>(base(K) + kk);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    dist[gIdx] = tDist[ty][tx];\n    path[gIdx] = tPath[ty][tx];\n}\n\n// Phase 3: all remaining tiles (I,J) with I != K and J != K. Both operands come\n// from the snapshots written in phases 1 and 2, so the k-steps are independent\n// of each other and only the cell's own value changes between steps.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TILE * TILE)\nfwPhase3(unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path, const unsigned int* colSnap,\n         const unsigned int* rowSnap, const size_t m, const size_t K) {\n    const size_t J = blockIdx.x;\n    const size_t I = blockIdx.y;\n    if (I == K || J == K) return;\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int colOp[TILE][TILE];  // colOp[i][kk] = d[I*TILE+i][k]\n    __shared__ unsigned int rowOp[TILE][TILE];  // rowOp[kk][j] = d[k][J*TILE+j]\n\n    const size_t ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t gRow = I * TILE + ty;\n    const size_t gCol = J * TILE + tx;\n    const size_t gIdx = gRow * m + gCol;\n\n    unsigned int curDist = dist[gIdx];\n    unsigned int curPath = path[gIdx];\n    colOp[ty][tx] = colSnap[gRow * TILE + tx];\n    rowOp[ty][tx] = rowSnap[ty * m + gCol];\n    __syncthreads();\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < TILE; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int newDist = colOp[ty][kk] + rowOp[kk][tx];\n        if (newDist < curDist) {\n            curDist = newDist;\n            curPath = static_cast<unsigned int>(K * TILE + kk);\n        }\n    }\n\n    dist[gIdx] = curDist;\n    path[gIdx] = curPath;\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n\n    // 1. Triangle inequality: dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] >= dist[i][j]\n    // Check a sample of paths to avoid O(n^3) validation time\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++j) {\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n\n                // Check for overflow before addition\n                if (distIK < INF && distKJ < INF) {\n                    if (distIK + distKJ < distIJ) {\n                        printf(\"Validation failed: triangle inequality violated at [%zu,%zu,%zu]\\n\",\n                               i, j, k);\n                        return false;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of nodes in the graph (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n// Runs Floyd-Warshall on the GPU as a blocked computation. Each tile is handled by one thread block of\n// TILE x TILE threads, one thread per matrix cell.\nconstexpr size_t TILE = 32;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                     \\\n    do {                                                                     \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                           \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                           \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                               \\\n            exit(1);                                                         \\\n        }                                                                    \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Index calculation for flattened 2D array\ninline constexpr size_t idx2(const size_t i, const size_t j, const size_t n) noexcept {\n    return j * n + i;\n}\n\nvoid initializeDistanceMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes,\n                              const unsigned int rangeMin, const unsigned int rangeMax) {\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - rangeMin) + 1.0;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes * numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[i] = rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n    }\n\n    // Set diagonal to zero (distance from node to itself is 0)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid initializePathMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            path[idx2(i, j, numNodes)] = j;\n            path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = i;\n        }\n        path[idx2(j, j, numNodes)] = j;\n    }\n}\n\n// Phase 1: the diagonal tile (K,K). Runs the k-steps of round K inside the tile.\n// Before each k-step it saves the diagonal's column k and row k so that the\n// other tiles of this round can read the values d[.][k] and d[k][.] exactly as\n// they were before step k.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TILE * TILE)\nfwPhase1(unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path, unsigned int* colSnap, unsigned int* rowSnap,\n         const size_t m, const size_t K) {\n    __shared__ unsigned int tDist[TILE][TILE];\n    __shared__ unsigned int tPath[TILE][TILE];\n\n    const size_t ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t base = K * TILE;\n    const size_t gIdx = (base + ty) * m + base + tx;\n\n    tDist[ty][tx] = dist[gIdx];\n    tPath[ty][tx] = path[gIdx];\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < TILE; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int distIK = tDist[ty][kk];\n        const unsigned int distKJ = tDist[kk][tx];\n        if (tx == 0) colSnap[(base + ty) * TILE + kk] = distIK;\n        if (ty == 0) rowSnap[kk * m + base + tx] = distKJ;\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n        if (newDist < tDist[ty][tx]) {\n            tDist[ty][tx] = newDist;\n            tPath[ty][tx] = static_cast<unsigned int>(base + kk);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    dist[gIdx] = tDist[ty][tx];\n    path[gIdx] = tPath[ty][tx];\n}\n\n// Phase 2: tiles (K,J) for J != K (blockIdx.y == 0) and tiles (I,K) for I != K\n// (blockIdx.y == 1), blockIdx.x holds the other block index. Each of these tiles\n// reads one operand from the diagonal snapshot (fixed for the round) and the\n// other operand from its own, sequentially updated, contents.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TILE * TILE)\nfwPhase2(unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path, unsigned int* colSnap, unsigned int* rowSnap,\n         const size_t m, const size_t K) {\n    const size_t t = blockIdx.x;\n    if (t == K) return;\n    const bool isRowTile = (blockIdx.y == 0);\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int tDist[TILE][TILE];\n    __shared__ unsigned int tPath[TILE][TILE];\n    __shared__ unsigned int tFixed[TILE][TILE];\n\n    const size_t ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t rowBase = isRowTile ? K * TILE : t * TILE;\n    const size_t colBase = isRowTile ? t * TILE : K * TILE;\n    const size_t gIdx = (rowBase + ty) * m + colBase + tx;\n\n    tDist[ty][tx] = dist[gIdx];\n    tPath[ty][tx] = path[gIdx];\n    // Row tile: d[i][k] for the rows of block K. Both operands come\n// from the snapshots written in phases 1 and 2, so the k-steps are independent\n// of each other and only the cell's own value changes between steps.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TILE * TILE)\nfwPhase3(unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path, const unsigned int* colSnap,\n         const unsigned int* rowSnap, const size_t m, const size_t K) {\n    const size_t J = blockIdx.x;\n    const size_t I = blockIdx.y;\n    if (I == K || J == K) return;\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int colOp[TILE][TILE];  // colOp[i][kk] = d[I*TILE+i][k]\n    __shared__ unsigned int rowOp[TILE][TILE];  // rowOp[kk][j] = d[k][J*TILE+j]\n\n    const size_t ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t gRow = I * TILE + ty;\n    const size_t gCol = J * TILE + tx;\n    const size_t gIdx = gRow * m + gCol;\n\n    unsigned int curDist = dist[gIdx];\n    unsigned int curPath = path[gIdx];\n    colOp[ty][tx] = colSnap[gRow * TILE + tx];\n    rowOp[ty][tx] = rowSnap[ty * m + gCol];\n    __syncthreads();\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < TILE; ++kk) {\n        const unsigned int newDist = colOp[ty][kk] + rowOp[kk][tx];\n        if (newDist < curDist) {\n            curDist = newDist;\n            curPath = static_cast<unsigned int>(K * TILE + kk);\n        }\n    }\n\n    dist[gIdx] = curDist;\n    path[gIdx] = curPath;\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n\n    // 1. Their k-steps come after all real k-steps and can\n// never shorten a real distance, so the real results are unchanged and the\n// padding is dropped when copying back.\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    const size_t tiles = (numNodes + TILE - 1) / TILE;\n    const size_t m = tiles * TILE;\n\n    std::vector<unsigned int> hostDist(m * m, INF);\n    std::vector<unsigned int> hostPath(m * m, 0);\n    for (size_t p = 0; p < m; ++p) {\n        hostDist[p * m + p] = 0;\n    }\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n            hostDist[i * m + j] = dist[i * numNodes + j];\n            hostPath[i * m + j] = path[i * numNodes + j];\n        }\n    }\n\n    unsigned int *dDist = nullptr, *dPath = nullptr, *dColSnap = nullptr, *dRowSnap = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dDist, m * m * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dPath, m * m * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dColSnap, m * TILE * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dRowSnap, TILE * m * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dDist, hostDist.data(), m * m * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dPath, hostPath.data(), m * m * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 block(TILE, TILE);\n    const dim3 phase2Grid(tiles, 2);\n    const dim3 phase3Grid(tiles, tiles);\n\n    // Each round K performs k-steps K*TILE .. each intermediate node k\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // For each source node i\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            // For each destination node j\n }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of Their k-steps come after all real k-steps and can\n// never shorten a real distance, so the real results are unchanged and the\n// padding is dropped when copying back.\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    const size_t tiles = (numNodes + TILE - 1) / TILE;\n    const size_t m = tiles * TILE;\n\n    std::vector<unsigned int> hostDist(m * m, INF);\n    std::vector<unsigned int> hostPath(m * m, 0);\n    for (size_t p = 0; p < m; ++p) {\n        hostDist[p * m + p] = 0;\n    }\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n            hostDist[i * m + j] = dist[i * numNodes + j];\n            hostPath[i * m + j] = path[i * numNodes + j];\n        }\n    }\n\n    unsigned int *dDist = nullptr, *dPath = nullptr, *dColSnap = nullptr, *dRowSnap = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dDist, m * m * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dPath, m * m * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dColSnap, m * TILE * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dRowSnap, TILE * m * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dDist, hostDist.data(), m * m * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dPath, hostPath.data(), m * m * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 block(TILE, TILE);\n    const dim3 phase2Grid(tiles, 2);\n    const dim3 phase3Grid(tiles, tiles);\n\n    // Each round K performs k-steps K*TILE .. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzazhXLGfs1waSdvXsag","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark now runs Floyd-Warshall on the GPU, unconditionally. Output matches the original CPU version at every size I tested, and the path matrix matches too.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- **`floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp`**: the CPU `floydWarshall` is replaced by a blocked GPU version with 32×32 tiles, one thread per cell. Each round runs three kernels: the diagonal tile, the row and column tiles, then all remaining tiles. Tiles stage their operands in shared memory. Tile edges are handled by padding the matrix to a multiple of 32 with INF, and the padding is dropped on copy-back. Input generation, validation, and `-r` output are unchanged.\n- **`floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`**: the project now enables CUDA, the `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA via `LANGUAGE CUDA`, and the executable is still `floydwarshall`. Minimum CMake is 3.24, and architectures default to `native` (overridable with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`).\n\nNo new files were created in the repo. The build is clean with no warnings.\n\n**Verification**\n\n- Distance hashes and min/max/sample values match the original binary for n = 0, 1, 2, 5, 31, 32, 33, 63, 100, 255, 512, 777, 1000, 1024, 1500. `-v` validation passes at 512, 2048, and 4096.\n- The path matrix is never printed, so I checked it separately with instrumented copies in `/tmp`. Its hashes also match the original at every size above.\n\n**Timings (RTX 3090)**\n\n| n | CPU original | GPU |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 166 ms | 6 ms |\n| 2048 | 9394 ms | 76 ms |\n| 4096 | — | 314 ms |\n\n**Choices to review**\n\n- The timer covers host-to-device copy, kernels, and device-to-host copy, but not CUDA context creation, which is warmed up before the timer starts. Timing kernels alone would look faster.\n- The GPU path has no CPU fallback, so the binary needs a CUDA device at runtime.\n- I did not try further tuning such as register-level tiling, so there is probably headroom beyond these numbers.\n- The repo is not a git repository, so I did not commit."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":720,"cache_read_input_tokens":63213,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":720},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7700b251-fb5d-4fed-bcf0-996d801777d4","uuid":"68ec95b7-8a95-4bfb-ab3e-0f15dc56be2c","timestamp":"2026-10-13T16:55:14.977Z","request_id":"req_011CfzazgzLJ5f29P6exT7KU"}
